theory.intro: A **multistage experiment** has two or more steps, such as tossing a coin and then spinning a spinner. Record every outcome in a **two-way array** or a **tree diagram** so that none is missed.
facts: A **multistage experiment** has two or more steps, and one result from every step together makes one **outcome**.

A **two-way array** suits two stages: one stage's results head the columns, the other's head the rows, and each allowed cell holds one outcome. When drawing without replacement, cross out impossible cells.
Order is part of the outcome, so $HT$ and $TH$ are different outcomes and both are recorded.
Keep separate objects as separate headings or branches, even when they share a label. Different cells or paths can then show the same recorded letters or numbers.
Multiply the stage counts when every branch at a stage has the same number of choices. This counts the complete paths, including separate choices that share a label.
Without replacement, remove only the object already drawn. Different objects can share a label, so matching labels may still occur.
steps: List the possible results of each stage.
Draw a two-way array or a tree diagram with one heading or branch for every result.
Write each complete outcome in its allowed cell or at the end of its path. When drawing without replacement, cross out impossible cells in the array.
Count the outcomes and check the count against the number of results at each stage.

workedExamples.question_text:
A wardrobe has long-sleeved ($L$) and short-sleeved ($S$) shirts, and red ($R$), black ($B$) and green ($G$) trousers.
One shirt and one pair of trousers are chosen. Record the shirt first.
a) Use a two-way array and list all the outfits.
b) State how many outfits there are and check the count.
workedExamples.solution_text:
a) Put the shirt results down the side and the trouser results across the top.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} & R & B & G \\ \hline L & (L,R) & (L,B) & (L,G) \\ S & (S,R) & (S,B) & (S,G) \end{array}$
Pair $L$ with each trouser result, then do the same for $S$.
The outfits are $(L,R)$, $(L,B)$, $(L,G)$, $(S,R)$, $(S,B)$ and $(S,G)$.
b) The array has $6$ cells.
Number of outfits:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2 \times 3\\&=6\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Three questions each have the answers Yes ($Y$) or No ($N$).
The answers are recorded in order.
a) Draw a tree diagram showing every outcome.
b) State how many outcomes there are and check the count.

Four separate cards show the letters M, O, O and N. Label the two O cards $O_1$ and $O_2$ so each card can be identified.
Two cards are drawn in order without replacement.
a) Record every ordered pair of cards in a two-way array, with the first draw down the side. Cross out the impossible cells.
b) How many ordered card draws are there? Check the count.
c) Why are some cells crossed out?
workedExamples.solution_text:
a) Cross out only the cells that use the same physical card twice.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} & M & O_1 & O_2 & N \\ \hline M & \times & (M,O_1) & (M,O_2) & (M,N) \\ O_1 & (O_1,M) & \times & (O_1,O_2) & (O_1,N) \\ O_2 & (O_2,M) & (O_2,O_1) & \times & (O_2,N) \\ N & (N,M) & (N,O_1) & (N,O_2) & \times \end{array}$
b) The $4$ diagonal cells are crossed out.
Number of ordered card draws:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}16-4\\&=12\end{aligned}$
Each first card leaves $3$ cards for the second draw, so $4 \times 3 = 12$.
c) The same physical card cannot be drawn twice because the first card is not replaced.
$(O_1,O_2)$ and $(O_2,O_1)$ use different cards, so these cells are allowed. Both give $OO$ when only the letters are recorded.

workedExamples.question_text:
Three cards showing the letters $B$, $A$ and $T$ are in a bag.
One card is drawn, then a second card is drawn without replacing the first.
Draw a tree diagram and list the outcomes to the right of the branches.

foundation.question_text:
A coin is tossed and a spinner with three equal sectors labelled $R$, $B$ and $G$ is spun.
The array records the outcomes, with the coin down the side and the spinner across the top.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} & R & B & G \\ \hline H & (H,R) & & (H,G) \\ T & (T,R) & (T,B) & \end{array}$
Write the outcomes that belong in the two empty cells.
foundation.solution_text:
Each cell pairs its row heading with its column heading.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} & R & B & G \\ \hline H & (H,R) & (H,B) & (H,G) \\ T & (T,R) & (T,B) & (T,G) \end{array}$
The missing outcomes are $(H,B)$ and $(T,G)$.

foundation.question_text:
A coin is tossed and a spinner with four equal sectors labelled $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$ is spun.
Use the empty array to record every outcome, then list them.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ \hline H & & & & \\ T & & & & \end{array}$
foundation.solution_text:
Every coin result pairs with every spinner result.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ \hline H & (H,1) & (H,2) & (H,3) & (H,4) \\ T & (T,1) & (T,2) & (T,3) & (T,4) \end{array}$
The outcomes are $(H,1)$, $(H,2)$, $(H,3)$, $(H,4)$, $(T,1)$, $(T,2)$, $(T,3)$ and $(T,4)$.

foundation.question_text:
Spinner $A$ has three equal sectors labelled $P$, $Q$ and $R$.
Spinner $B$ has five equal sectors labelled $1$ to $5$.
Both spinners are spun and Spinner $A$'s result is written first.
$\begin{array}{c|ccccc} & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 \\ \hline P & (P,1) & (P,2) & (P,3) & (P,4) & (P,5) \\ Q & (Q,1) & (Q,2) & (Q,3) & (Q,4) & (Q,5) \\ R & (R,1) & (R,2) & (R,3) & (R,4) & (R,5) \end{array}$
How many outcomes does this experiment have?
foundation.solution_text:
Each row is one result of Spinner $A$, each column is one result of Spinner $B$, and every cell holds one outcome.
Number of outcomes $= 3 \times 5$
$= 15$

Each complete path from the start is one outcome.
There are $6$ complete paths, so there are $6$ outcomes.
Number of outcomes $= 3 \times 2$
$= 6$

foundation.question_text:
Three cards showing the letters $C$, $A$ and $T$ are in a bag.
One card is drawn, then a second card is drawn without replacing the first.
The crosses show that the same card cannot be drawn twice.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} & C & A & T \\ \hline C & \times & (C,A) & \\ A & & \times & \\ T & & & \times \end{array}$
Complete the array and list all the outcomes.
foundation.solution_text:
Every cell except the crossed ones pairs its row letter with a different column letter.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} & C & A & T \\ \hline C & \times & (C,A) & (C,T) \\ A & (A,C) & \times & (A,T) \\ T & (T,C) & (T,A) & \times \end{array}$
The outcomes are $(C,A)$, $(C,T)$, $(A,C)$, $(A,T)$, $(T,C)$ and $(T,A)$.

foundation.question_text:
A spinner has three equal sectors labelled $1$, $2$ and $3$.
It is spun twice and both results are recorded in order.
Use the empty array to record every outcome, then list them.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline 1 & & & \\ 2 & & & \\ 3 & & & \end{array}$

development.question_text:
Spinner $A$ has four equal sectors labelled $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$.
Spinner $B$ has three equal sectors labelled $W$, $X$ and $Y$.
Both spinners are spun and Spinner $A$'s result is written first.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} & W & X & Y \\ \hline 1 & (1,W) & (1,X) & (1,Y) \\ 2 & (2,W) & & \\ 3 & & & \\ 4 & & & (4,Y) \end{array}$
Complete the array and state how many outcomes there are.
development.solution_text:
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} & W & X & Y \\ \hline 1 & (1,W) & (1,X) & (1,Y) \\ 2 & (2,W) & (2,X) & (2,Y) \\ 3 & (3,W) & (3,X) & (3,Y) \\ 4 & (4,W) & (4,X) & (4,Y) \end{array}$
The array has $4$ rows and $3$ columns.
Number of outcomes $= 4 \times 3$
$= 12$

development.question_text:
A coin is tossed, then a spinner with three equal sectors labelled $1$, $2$ and $3$ is spun, then the coin is tossed again.
Each outcome is recorded as (first toss, spin, second toss).
How many outcomes are there in total?
development.solution_text:
Each first toss has $3$ possible spinner results, and each of those has $2$ possible second-toss results.
Number of outcomes $= 2 \times 3 \times 2$
$= 12$

development.question_text:
A coin is tossed and a spinner with five equal sectors labelled $1$ to $5$ is spun.
$\begin{array}{c|ccccc} & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 \\ \hline H & & & & & \\ T & & & & & \end{array}$
State the total number of outcomes.
development.solution_text:
Each of the $2$ rows holds $5$ cells.
Number of outcomes $= 2 \times 5$
$= 10$

There are $8$ complete paths, so there are $8$ outcomes.
Number of outcomes $= 2 \times 2 \times 2$
$= 8$

development.question_text:
Spinner $A$ has two equal sectors labelled $R$ and $B$.
Spinner $B$ has four equal sectors labelled $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$.
Both spinners are spun and Spinner $A$'s result is written first.
Use a two-way array to list every outcome and state how many there are.
development.solution_text:
Pair each result of Spinner $A$ with every result of Spinner $B$ in turn.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ \hline R & (R,1) & (R,2) & (R,3) & (R,4) \\ B & (B,1) & (B,2) & (B,3) & (B,4) \end{array}$
The outcomes are $(R,1)$, $(R,2)$, $(R,3)$, $(R,4)$, $(B,1)$, $(B,2)$, $(B,3)$ and $(B,4)$.
Number of outcomes $= 2 \times 4$
$= 8$

mastery.question_text:
A spinner has three equal sectors labelled $1$, $2$ and $3$.
It is spun three times and the results are recorded in order.
How many outcomes are there in total?
mastery.solution_text:
Each spin has $3$ possible results, and each path splits into $3$ branches at the next spin.
Number of outcomes $= 3 \times 3 \times 3$
$= 27$

mastery.question_text:
A spinner has four equal sectors labelled $J$, $K$, $L$ and $M$.
It is spun twice and the results are recorded in order.
Use a two-way array to list every outcome and state how many there are.
mastery.solution_text:
Put the first spin down the side and the second spin across the top.
$\begin{array}{c|cccc} & J & K & L & M \\ \hline J & (J,J) & (J,K) & (J,L) & (J,M) \\ K & (K,J) & (K,K) & (K,L) & (K,M) \\ L & (L,J) & (L,K) & (L,L) & (L,M) \\ M & (M,J) & (M,K) & (M,L) & (M,M) \end{array}$
The same letter can occur twice, and reversing two different letters gives a different outcome.
The outcomes are $(J,J)$, $(J,K)$, $(J,L)$, $(J,M)$, $(K,J)$, $(K,K)$, $(K,L)$, $(K,M)$, $(L,J)$, $(L,K)$, $(L,L)$, $(L,M)$, $(M,J)$, $(M,K)$, $(M,L)$ and $(M,M)$.
Number of outcomes $= 4 \times 4$
$= 16$

mastery.question_text:
Four cards showing the letters $E$, $A$, $S$ and $T$ are in a bag.
One card is drawn, then a second card is drawn without replacing the first.
a. Set the outcomes out in a two-way array, crossing out the cells that cannot occur.
b. How many outcomes are there?
mastery.solution_text:
a. $\begin{array}{c|cccc} & E & A & S & T \\ \hline E & \times & (E,A) & (E,S) & (E,T) \\ A & (A,E) & \times & (A,S) & (A,T) \\ S & (S,E) & (S,A) & \times & (S,T) \\ T & (T,E) & (T,A) & (T,S) & \times \end{array}$
b. The array has $16$ cells and $4$ of them are crossed out.
Number of outcomes $= 16 - 4$
$= 12$
